_comment: Visual identity for your resume and cover letter. Onboarding writes a filled copy to user-library/format.json. Both generate_resume.py and build_cover_letter.py read it, so the two documents always look like a matched set. All keys are optional — anything omitted falls back to a clean default. Fonts must be installed on the machine that exports the PDF (LibreOffice); if a font is missing it silently substitutes, so prefer common fonts unless you know the font is present.
_color_help: Colors are 6-digit hex, no leading #. text_color = name/company/body (near-black reads best). muted_color = role titles, dates, contact line. rule_color = the hairline section dividers. accent_color = links (portfolio, projects, cover-letter website).
_font_help: name_font is the display font for the name only; body_font is everything else. Pick a name_font you actually have installed. Safe cross-platform display fonts: Georgia, Garamond, Cambria. Safe body fonts: Calibri, Arial, Helvetica.
_max_pages_help: Target resume length in pages (default 1). One page is right for most roles; set 2 for fields where a longer resume is standard (academic CV, federal, senior/technical). The RUN step passes this to page_count.py as --max-pages so the one-page loop enforces YOUR target, not a hardcoded 1.
